A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Full-text comparison and rendered-page checks support matching the main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–L, including material shifted by the added appendix paragraph.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark accuracy for SAE-based and SAE-free steering in Tables 1–2, along with activation analyses, sensitivity results, and generated examples.

after.justification: v3 retains these original benchmark results and supplementary analyses. Retention from v1 does not change their empirical status.

M1.justification: VS Decomposition, SAE feature selection, residual-activation steering, and the SAE-free eigenvector procedure are unchanged, including the feature-selection adjustment in Appendix B.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GSM8K, MATH levels 3–4, MMLU high-school mathematics, and MathOAI with the same supplementary data usage. The new mention of code and logical reasoning does not introduce evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same comparisons: original prompting for SAE-based steering, and original prompting, BoostStep, and MathNeuro for SAE-free steering. The new baseline discussion adds no comparator.

E3.justification: The 300-example GSM8K subset, feature-extraction sample, evaluated models, generation limits, GPT-4.1 judging, steering layers, and baseline settings remain unchanged in Sections 3 and 5 and Appendices A–D.

E4.justification: Reasoning-length, steering-strength, attention, reconstruction, orthogonality, eigenvector, and feature-ranking analyses are retained unchanged, as are the steering cases. The added paragraph supplies discussion without additional tests or comparative case outputs.

E5.justification: Accuracy reporting and the Spearman correlation analysis are unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests that are added or revised in the other.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plots, and displayed generated answers are unchanged. Appendix L newly reports qualitative assertions about irrelevant BoostStep output, reduced MathNeuro reasoning/self-reflection, and generation-speed differences, without adding supporting comparative traces or timing measurements.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, sparsity and orthogonality assumptions, steering derivation, and Appendix E proof are unchanged, as is the gradient-weighted feature formulation in Appendix K.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about extracting reasoning features from vanilla CoT and steering models with or without pretrained SAEs.

C2.justification: Appendix L adds a proposed explanation linking BoostStep hallucinations to irrelevant retrieval and asserts broader SAE-free applicability to code and logical reasoning. The existing limitations still describe broader reasoning-domain evaluation as future work.

D1.justification: SAE checkpoint identifiers, generation settings, feature indices, steering-strength recommendations, baseline implementation parameters, prompts, and resource links remain unchanged. The new efficiency assertions provide no additional implementation or timing details.

R1.justification: References and the related-work section are unchanged. The new Appendix L paragraph nevertheless sharpens positioning against BoostStep and MathNeuro by emphasizing their alleged drawbacks and claiming wider applicability for SAE-free steering.

P1.justification: v3 adds one short appendix paragraph, corrects affiliation numbering, and changes the listed Baidu affiliation to Microsoft. The remaining prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added discussion slightly reflows Appendix L and continues onto a mostly empty page before the remaining case tables. Literal double-asterisk formatting appears in the paragraph; existing figures, table structures, and captions are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Affiliation numbering is corrected, but the new Appendix L discussion weakens evidential precision: it refers to a BoostStep example absent from the accompanying SAE-based case table and asserts speed and cross-domain advantages without supporting results. Its awkward formatting and nearly empty continuation page also reduce presentation quality. The unchanged technical content limits the deterioration.
